la:adj:obvius.gloss: in the way, who goes or comes to meet
senses: in the way, who goes or comes to meet
la:adj:obvius.html:
obvĭus, a, um, adj.
ob-via
,
in the way, so as to meet, meeting, to meet (class.).
In gen.: si ille obvius ei futurus omnino non erat,had no expectation of meeting him,: dare se obvium alicui,to meet a person,: quo in loco inter se obvii fuissent,had met each other,: libellus insidiarum ab obvio quodam porrectus,by one who met him,; cf. : cuicumque est obvia,whomsoever she meets,: cui mater mediā sese tulit obvia silvā,met,: obvia cui Camilla Occurrit,: esse in obvio alicui, to be in the way of or where one can meet another, ; so, with ellips. of dat.: Brutidius meus ad Martis fuit obvius aram,: se gravissimis tempestatibus obvium ferre,: agmen obviorum,: obvii e diverso,.—Of things: neque aranei tenvia fila Obvia sentimus,: simulacra nobis,: obvias mihi litteras mittas,send to meet,; cf. : ultroque ferebant Obvia securis ubera lactis oves,offered, presented,: montes, qui obvii erant itineri adversariorum, which lay in their way, which they met or fell in with, : quaeque,: obvia flamina,: obvius undis,up the stream,: obviaque hospitiis teneat frondentibus arbos,over against, opposite,: aquilones,contrary, adverse,: prona cadit lateque et cominus obvia frangens,every thing in its way,.—
In partic.
In a bad sense, as an enemy, against, to meet or encounter: si ingredienti cum armatā manu obvius fueris,: Jugurthae obvius procedit,: obvii hostibus,: infestā subit obvius hastā,.—
In a good sense.
Easy of access, affable, courteous (perh. not ante-Aug.): est enim obvius, et expositus, plenusque humanitate,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things, at hand, easy, ready, obvious: nec se obvias fuisse dicenti, sed conquisitas (figuras),: quidquid venerit obvium loquamur,: obvias opes deferre deos,: comitas,: laudes,common,: obvia et illaborata virtus,easy, not difficult of attainment,: ex obvio fere victus (animalibus),.—
Of words, in constant use, common: est vestibulum in sermonibus celebre atque obvium verbum,: municipes et municipia sunt verba dictu facilia et usu obvia,; ; cf.: obvium est dicere dimidiā,.—
Se dare obvium, to occur to one's mind or memory: licet omnes (versus) praesens memoria non suggerat, tamen, qui se dederint obvios, annotabo,.—
Lying open, i. e. exposed, obnoxious to an evil (poet.): rupes Obvia ventorum furiis expostaque ponto,: melioribus opto Auspiciis et quae fuerit minus obvia Graiis,: calvitium quoquoversus obvium,i. e. exposed to the air,

la:adv:obviam.html:
ob-vĭam (also written separate, ob vĭam; cf. Corss. Ausspr. I. 495, 769), adv.
Lit., in the way; hence, with verbs of motion (in a good or bad sense), towards, against, to meet: ob Trojam duxit exercitum pro ad, similiterque vadimonium obisse, id est ad vadimonium isse, et obviam ad viam, Paul. ex Müll.: morti occumbant obviam, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 176 Vahl.): nec quisquam tam audax fuat homo, qui obviam obsistat mihi,as to put himself in my way,: cum in Cumanum mihi obviam venisti,: prodire,; cf.: si quā ex parte obviam contra veniretur, an advance or attack should be made, : alicui obviam advenire, C. Gracch. ap. : quem quaero, optime ecce obviam mihi est,is coming to meet me,: fit obviam Clodio ante fundum ejus,meets,: obviam ire alicui,to go to meet, et saep.: obviam procedere alicui,to go to meet,: prodire alicui,: properare,: proficisci,: exire,: progredi,: mittere,to send to meet,: se offerre,to go to meet, to meet,: effundi,to pour out to meet, to go in great numbers to meet,: de obviam itione ita faciam,; late Lat., also, in obviam: ecce exercitus in obviam illis,.—
Trop., at hand, within reach: nec sycophantiis, nec fucis ullum mantellum obviam est,: in comitio estote obviam,: tibi nulla aegritudo est animo obviam,: amanti mihi tot obviam eveniunt morae,present themselves, interpose,: ire periculis,to meet courageously, to encounter them,: cupiditati hominum obviam ire,to resist, oppose,; so, ire superbiae nobilitatis,: ire sceleri,: ire injuriae,: ire irae,: ire fraudibus,: crimini,.—Also, in a good sense, to meet an evil, i. e. to remedy, prevent it: ni Caesar obviam isset, tribuendo pecunias pro modo detrimenti,: infecunditati terrarum,: timori,: dedecori,.

la:verb:obverto.html:
ob-verto, ti, sum, 3, v. a.
To turn

towards or against, to direct towards any thing (not in Cic. or Cæs.): cujus ob os Graii ora obvertebant sua, Poët. ap. ; also ap. : mihi cornua,: arcūs in aliquem,: fenestras in aquilonem,: pelago proras,; without pelago: cornua velatarum obvertimus antennarum,direct,: obstantes dum vult obvertere remos, to turn against (the water), to play, : ordines ad clamorem,.—

Mid., to turn one's self to or towards, turn to any thing: obvertor ad undas,.—Hence, obversus, a, um, P. a., turned towards or against, directed towards.
Lit.: faciemque obversus in agmen utrumque,: ad matrem,: domicilia (apium) ad orientem,; for which: frons (ornithonis) orienti,: Caucasus quā soli est obversus,.—With simple acc.: obversus orientem,; cf.: profligatis obversis,the opponents, enemy,.—
Trop., turned towards, inclined to, engaged in: ad sanguinem, et caedes,: obversi militum studiis,.

la:verb:obvio.html:
ob-vĭo, āvi, 1, v. n.,
to meet (post-class.).
In gen.: alicui,: sibi,.—
In partic.
In a hostile sense, to withstand, resist, oppose: alicui,: suae confessioni,.—
To prevent, hinder, obviate: grandini,: vermibus,.

la:verb:obvenio.gloss: to come before or in the way of, meet, come face-to-face
senses: to come before or in the way of, meet, come face-to-face
to come or fall to someone, fall to the lot of
la:verb:obvenio.html:
ob-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. n.
Lit., to come before or in the way of, to meet (syn.: obviam venio, occurro; perh. only in the foll. passage): se in tempore pugnae obventurum,would come up to the fight, join in the battle,.—
Transf.
To come or fall to one; to fall to one's lot; usually referring only to what is accidental, as the result of a lot, etc.: Syria Scipioni,: legati, quibus hae partes ad defendendum obvenerant,: tibi obvenit iste labos,: Aemilio novum bellum in Etruriā sorte obvenit,: cui classis obvenisset,.—But also in gen.: cum hereditas ei obvenisset, (dub.; Orell. and B. and K. venisset): si istiusmodi mi fundus hereditate obvenerit,: cum obvenisset mihi hereditas,; ; ; : haud ab re tibi istic obvenit labos,.—
Still more gen., like obtingere, of an event, to fall out, to befall, happen, occur to one: obvenit occasio,: vitium (at the auspices),; : quaecumque obvenissent,: obveniens lucrum,.

la:verb:obvolvo.gloss: to wrap around, cover all over, muffle up; smother
senses: to wrap around, cover all over, muffle up; smother
la:verb:obvolvo.html:
ob-volvo, vi, ūtum, 3, v. a.,
to wrap round, muffle up, cover all over (class.; cf. obtego).
Lit.: pictor ille vidit, obvolvendum caput Agamemnonis esse,; so freq.: capite obvoluto,with his head muffled up,; ; ; cf. ; : caput obnubere ... quod est obvolvere, Paul. ex Müll.: os obvolutum est folliculo,: bracchium lanis fasciisque,.—
Transf.: fax obvoluta sanguine, covered, Enn. ap. ( Vahl.).—*
Trop.: verbisque decoris Obvolvas vitium,cloak, disguise,: obvolutus in peccatis,.

la:verb:obversor.html:
ob-versor, ātus, 1, v. dep. (
act. collat. form obverso, āre, acc. to P.), to take position opposite or over against, to oppose one's self (class.).
Lit.: magnam partem eorum palam Carthagini obversari dici,: in foro,: sedebant judices, obversabantur advocati,: limini,who were about the threshold,: in urbe inter coetus,.—
Trop., to hover or float before, to appear to one: illius et nomen dulce obversatur ad aures,: mihi ante oculos obversatur rei publicae dignitas,: obversentur species honestae viro,: animis, oculis,: in somnis,: sibi speciem noctibus obversari,.—
To oppose, withstand, resist (eccl. Lat.): malo obniti et obversari,.
